title: Montuno, clave and Gospel rhythm demonstrated
summary: He explains Latin accents on the second beat, the clave, Calypso and Bossa Nova.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: When you play Latin, you come near Gospel music. That's the closest thing to the...between the Latin rhythms

and the so-called Gospel Rock-and-Roll. If you play that, you come close to that. See now, in Latin you have two beats. There's the first accent on the first beat, you know, and then, when you get to the part they call the "montuno," which is the newest(?), where you take off or... (How do you say it? You've got a difference in...)...where you really get into the rhythm, you know... You start the beat on the second...you start your rhythm on the second beat.
You do that in the montuno?

In the montuno you start on the second beat. You can trace that to Calypso -- same thing. And now Brazil came up with the Bossa Nova, which is the same beat spread over two bars. See? Let me see...Latin...

The only thing is that the bass... The bass will give you the fundamental in the (?). And then you have a metronome type of thing which is not syncopated; it's just a straight beat. But you syncopate around that...
Well, what is that played on?

Well, at one time you used to have a thing called the clave, two sticks that will give you the pulse. [DEMONSTRATES CLAVE] Now, in order to play the montuno you start on the second beat: One, [THEN PLAYS CLAVE], One, [THEN PLAYS CLAVE]. You see? The other straight one is
You notice I start on the one; the montuno is on the second. [PLAYS ONE-TWO-TWO]
So in a way, it almost starts (?)s with the (?).
Yeah. But also, in Jazz you will play like the first chord very often harmonodically(?), and then when you get to the second now you're going to break off, and the rhythm...
Yeah, you change the rhythm to another cymbal or anything, but you're still on the same beat.
The same pulse. Only you put more into it. But you change the color, I would say.
